FRQs REVIEWED AND RE-PUSHED 2026-09-30 (second pass on 1917885 q7 and 1917886 q11, after an independent read-only review of the first push). The review found real defects in the first version and all are fixed and re-pushed. (1) q11's group labels are not all singular - Class A / Shop A are, Sophomores / Seniors are not - and the model answer used singular verbs and pronouns throughout, so the sleep context read 'Sophomores is roughly symmetric: its mean ... Seniors are more spread out ... Its standard deviation'. Every verb, possessive and subject now comes from per-context arrays (verb_is, verb_get, verb_have, poss, poss_cap, subj). (2) The comparison sentence I added to the shape/center target was BACKWARDS for the exam context: it said Class A's typical score is higher when Class B's median is the higher one. Caught by simulating all 3 contexts x 7 random shifts against the displayed numbers, not by eye. (3) q7's stem said "Barista A's daily sales numbers averaged 34 drinks sold per day" and "Driver A's daily delivery counts averaged 34 packages delivered per day" - plural noun inside a singular slot, so two of three variants were visibly broken English on the student's screen. The array is now singular ('sales count', 'delivery count'). (4) q7's three prompt bullets did not map one-to-one onto the three rubric categories (two bullets landed on Standard Deviation, Practical Conclusion had none); there are now three bullets, one per category. (5) q7's instructor line 'name the statistic it rests on (the standard deviation)' handed the student rubric's answer away and broke parity with it; both now say 'name the statistic your conclusion rests on'. (6) Smaller wording fixes: 'steadier' -> 'more consistent' to match the taught word, 'a few very low scores that make its results far more spread out' -> 'its scores are far more spread out, including a few very low ones' (the old wording asserted a cause the five-number summary cannot show), the plural 'unusual low scores' removed because a summary can only reveal the single most extreme value, 'a typical week looks the same' -> 'on average ... come out the same', 'on any given week' -> 'from week to week', 'variability' -> 'spread' in the description, and q11's spread bullet now matches what the rubric actually scores. FRQs REWRITTEN AND PUSHED 2026-09-30 (slot 9 = qid 1917885 q7, slot 10 = qid 1917886 q11; library qsetids are attached to THIS test only, so no other assessment changed). Rewritten for plain language, and pushed to the MOM library in cid 334437. q7: the student checklist used to state the answers ('Say what a smaller standard deviation means: those values sit close to their mean, so they are consistent', 'which group is more reliable'); it now asks for the underlying observation instead, 'reliable' is out of the file entirely, and the prompt no longer says 'even though their means are identical' or 'Which group is more reliable'. The instructor rubric and the model answer were rewritten in the SAME pass so the two rubrics carry identical categories, identical point values and one line per line, with the grader targets moved into $t_* variables instead of being typed inline. q11 (slot 10) was REBUILT on q7's scaffold because it was the only ch2 FRQ still on the legacy layout, which is why slot 10 did not follow slot 9's question setup: truncated $css_block with no details-toggle JS (the arrow never switched and the box stayed at max-height 0), a hand-written instructor rubric with no point labels and no .ideal-ans targets, and no 'be sure to address' bullets. Four real defects went with it: the summary table HANDED OVER the answer in a Shape column ('left-skewed with a low outlier near 3 hrs') while the rubric asked the student to describe the shape; the scenario said 'weekly hours of sleep' and meant nightly; the seniors row called itself left-skewed while its mean (6.2) sat ABOVE its median (6.0); and the rubric offered 'standard deviation or IQR' with no quartiles in the table, so the IQR option was unanswerable. Now: mean / median / SD / min / Q1 / Q3 / max (IQR computable), no shape column, three pre-built contexts whose numbers are internally consistent (mean-vs-median side, outlier side and 1.5 x IQR fences all checked over all 3 x 7 random shifts), plus a shared random shift per draw so two students rarely see the same numbers, and $css_block copied verbatim from reference/free-response-template.php.
